title: STREAMINGGS: Voxel-Based Streaming 3D Gaussian Splatting with Memory Optimization and Architectural Support
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) struggles to achieve real-time 90 FPS rendering on mobile devices (currently only 2-9 FPS), with existing accelerators optimizing compute efficiency but ignoring memory efficiency, resulting in redundant DRAM traffic.
motivation: 3DGS is efficient for 3D rendering but memory bandwidth is the primary bottleneck on resource-constrained mobile devices, not compute.
method: STREAMINGGS implements fully streaming algorithm-architecture co-design with fine-grained pipelining and transforms from tile-centric rendering (tile-first, load all Gaussians) to memory-centric rendering (stream Gaussian groups, load only touched tiles). This approach reduces DRAM traffic and enables better prefetching and memory utilization on mobile GPUs.
key_novelty: Shift from tile-centric to memory-centric rendering paradigm with streaming architecture enables fine-grained pipelining and dramatically reduces DRAM bandwidth requirements for mobile 3DGS inference.
contributions: Memory-centric rendering architecture replacing tile-centric approach to reduce DRAM traffic
Fully streaming algorithm design enabling fine-grained pipelining
Architectural support for efficient DRAM access patterns
45.7x speedup and 62.9x energy savings vs Ampere GPU on mobile

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 62.9x energy savings vs mobile Ampere GPU

limitations: Abstract does not discuss comparison with other 3D rendering accelerators, quality/visual fidelity preservation, or scalability to very large Gaussian sets.
primary_theme: Memory-centric streaming 3DGS accelerator for mobile rendering
